chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"The Mudabbir (a slave man freed by his master upon his death) is from the one-third [of the estate]." And he said, "For a man to reclaim [from the bequest] his one-third, if he had bequeathed [more] during health or illness."

key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: The one-third portion of the estate reserved for bequests
key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرُ: A slave man whose master stipulates he will be freed upon the master's death

ai.seo_question: What is the share of a Mudabbir slave in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the financial mechanics of *Mudabbir* manumission, establishing that the slave's freedom is funded from the one-third of the estate allocated for bequests (*al-thuluth*). It further grants the master the right to reclaim any excess amount paid from this share if the bequest exceeded the standard limit, a ruling applicable whether the stipulation was made during health or illness. This highlights the Shia juristic view of *Mudabbir* as a conditional bequest rather than an immediate transfer of ownership.
